newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MAY 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The drachmas came under pressure yesterday for the first time in a while as 400 million US dollars left the country - sources at the Bank of Greece say the outflows were due to American investors cashing in state bonds. However, the BoG appears unconcerned, considering to a degree desirable that such "speculative" capital depart.
--The Agricultural Bank has 470 billion drachmas worth of unpaid debts, more than 25 percent of its total lending.
--EU member-states have agreed to work together to combat the phenomenon of corruption and bribery in the public sector.

--Banks will lift the confidentiality clause on those clients with debts to IKA, the social security foundation, as part of efforts to gather contributions owed by employers. The measure is included in a bill to be submitted to Parliament by the labour ministry.
--The upward swing of the Athens Stock Exchange is all to the benefit of the state - the finance ministry is to receive 40-50 billion drachmas from the transfer of a bond loan to shares.

--The administration of the state-run Agricultural Bank of Greece have characterised the bank's financial problems both in its balance sheet and portfolio as a blow to the servicing of the public debt.
--Taxation imposed on interest earned on state titles will double to 15.0 percent as of January 1998, according to reports. NAFTEMBORIKI

--The government is keeping its cards close to its chest on anything regarding its plans for changes to the job market, to be discussed with unions and emploers. Yesterday, the three decided what would not be discussed during the talks, which begin June 18.
--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, is expected to rubber-stamp a special investment plan worth 135 billion drachmas for 1997-1998.
--The bourse will give free rein to trading in Xiosbank shares today, lifting yesterday's 20 percent ceiling.

--Competitiveness of firms at the present conjuncture will be the focus of today's Federation of Greek Industries general assembly. Speakers will include Prime Minister Costas Simitis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

--Transport Minister Haris Kastanidis yesterday proposed that the purchase of airplanes to upgrade Olympic Airways fleet be overseen by Parliament. OA, Greece's national carrier, plans to spend 600 billion drachmas on two Boeing and two Airbus. The programme foresees the purchase of 10 Airbus 340 and 25 Boeings by 2005. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
